title: carol joins, then alice plays, optimized

timeline.label: Carol joins the game. `len`, the length of her name, sits on the stack. `name` isn't copied anywhere. The compiler's data points straight at the name's bytes in the call data, using their offset and length, saved in memory.
Carol's join is done. Her name is in her record in storage: one slot holds its length, two hold its bytes.
Alice plays. The code copies her player record from storage into memory, and `player` now lives there.

The optimizer has inlined `_applyCombo`: its code runs right here, with no real call. The compiler's data still marks where the call begins, so only `_applyCombo`'s own variables are listed. `mult` has no location yet.
`mult` now has a location: 8 bytes of memory.
`mult = combo` doesn't copy anything. The compiler's data points `mult` at the same memory word as `combo`: `combo` uses the word's last 4 bytes, and `mult`, a wider type, uses its last 8.
Back in `_turn`. `_applyCombo`'s variables are gone, and `gained`, the result it returned, now has a location in memory.
